title: UK Stopping Distances: The Highway Code Chart Explained
seoTitle: Highway Code Stopping Distances: 20–70 mph Chart & Tips
excerpt: Thinking, braking and total stopping distances from 20 to 70 mph, and how to remember them for the theory test.
description: The Highway Code stopping distances from 20 to 70 mph explained: thinking and braking distance, wet and icy roads, the two-second rule and how to remember them.
body:
Stopping distances come up in the UK theory test, and they matter on the road too. The Highway Code gives typical figures for a car in good conditions. Here they are, with an easy way to remember them.

## Thinking, braking and stopping distance

- **Thinking distance** is how far you travel between seeing a hazard and pressing the brake.
- **Braking distance** is how far you travel once the brakes are on.
- **Stopping distance** is the two added together.

## The Highway Code figures

- **20 mph:** 6 m thinking + 6 m braking = 12 m (about 3 car lengths)
- **30 mph:** 9 m thinking + 14 m braking = 23 m (about 6 car lengths)
- **40 mph:** 12 m thinking + 24 m braking = 36 m (about 9 car lengths)
- **50 mph:** 15 m thinking + 38 m braking = 53 m (about 13 car lengths)
- **60 mph:** 18 m thinking + 55 m braking = 73 m (about 18 car lengths)
- **70 mph:** 21 m thinking + 75 m braking = 96 m (about 24 car lengths)

## A simple way to remember them

Thinking distance goes up by 3 m for every 10 mph: 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21. If you remember that, you only need to learn the braking distances. Notice how braking distance grows much faster than speed: at 70 mph it is more than ten times the braking distance at 20 mph.

## Wet and icy roads

- On wet roads, stopping distances can be at least double
- On icy roads, braking distances can be up to ten times longer

## The two-second rule

On the road, it's easier to keep a time gap than to judge metres. Leave at least a two-second gap to the vehicle in front on a fast road in good conditions. Double it on wet roads, and leave even more on icy roads.

## Practise for the theory test
